results.summary_before: This is an analog voltage-controlled oscillator built from four differential stages with capacitive loading, providing eight output taps with phase differences. The frequency is controlled by a bias current or voltage applied to an analog input pin, and the eight tap signals are buffered to digital outputs. It requires external DC power for control and an oscilloscope for monitoring. Silicon tests show it works, achieving frequencies from 33 kHz to 2.8 MHz depending on bias current, with measured phase relationships among the taps.

results.summary_before: This design implements a simple stream cipher that XORs an 8-bit data input with the output of a linear-feedback shift register. The LFSR value is also provided on the bidirectional pins so that the encrypted output can be decrypted externally by XORing with the same value. The design was verified in simulation by manually calculating LFSR states and checking the encrypted output against expected values. No external hardware is required, and the project is a straightforward demonstration of LFSR-based encryption.

results.summary_before: This project is a 4-bit up/down binary counter with enable and test mode. It uses input pins for test, up/down selection, and enable, and outputs the 4-bit count value. Testing requires connecting the enable pin to VDD, test to GND, up/down to a switch, reset to an RC startup circuit, and a 50 MHz clock, with the outputs connected to LEDs. The design is a straightforward digital building block with minimal documentation beyond basic operation.
